items.snippet: UNSW engineers have identified a number of chemicals that may merit closer scrutiny to ensure water utility companies and regulators can make informed decisions about the management of biosolids.

items.title: Astronomers deliver the sharpest and deepest view yet of the low-frequency radio sky
items.snippet: Using the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR), an international team led by Leiden University has produced the sharpest and most sensitive radio image of the sky ever made at low radio frequencies. The image reveals almost 63,000 radio sources, such as active galactic nuclei and star-forming galaxies, across a patch of sky about 25 times the area of the full moon. items.title: Children may be missing out on free school meals as families favor private education, study finds
items.snippet: Children in some of India's poorest families may be missing out on free school meals because the scheme does not match parents' aspirations for their futures, new research has revealed.

items.title: Twisted atomic layers slide spontaneously at room temperature in simulations
items.snippet: Researchers revealed an ultralow-barrier collective sliding mechanism mediated by domain walls, as well as defect-induced pinning of the sliding motion. They found that twisted bilayer MoS₂ moiré superlattices can undergo spontaneous long-range interlayer sliding at room temperature, while a sulfur-vacancy concentration of only about 0.1% can turn the motion into localized oscillations.

items.title: Climate shapes microbial nitrogen pump in forests, not in farmlands
items.snippet: Microbes build a long-lived nitrogen reservoir in soil from the remains of dead bacteria and fungi, which cling to minerals and resist decay. The microbial nitrogen pump turns nitrogen taken up by living microbes into this persistent pool, and microbial nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) has long been assumed to regulate this process.

items.title: Societies could lose ability to respond to climate change
items.snippet: Human societies could lose the ability to respond to worsening climate change, scientists have warned.

items.title: Paired DNA strands recognize shape, not just sequence, in new small-molecule sensing method
items.snippet: You have probably performed a sandwich assay before, even if you didn't know it. Sandwich assays are the molecular sensing technology behind lateral flow tests like the at-home COVID test. After a sample is dripped onto the test strip, it combines with detector antibodies attached to tiny gold particles, which bind to any viral proteins present. items.title: Underwater cameras can estimate fish weight in real time without generating full depth maps
items.snippet: Accurate fish-weight estimates can help aquaculture operators manage feeding, monitor growth and plan harvests. However, conventional underwater imaging methods often require substantial computing power and can struggle with reflections, bubbles and turbid water.
